title: GeneXpert MTB/RIF as a named cartridge platform
dek: Wikipedia's GeneXpert MTB/RIF page is the instrument/cartridge node. Ultra trace calls, silent RRDR SNPs, and WRD policy stay on tb-xpert-ultra.
story: GeneXpert MTB/RIF on Wikipedia (Q5531060) is a named closed PCR/melt cartridge on a Cepheid instrument that detects MTBC DNA and interrogates rpoB for rifampin resistance. The encyclopedia node is the platform story (development, WHO endorsement as a WRD class).

Simplfy's tb-xpert-ultra plate is the assay you actually interpret: IS6110/IS1081, trace, I491F outside the window, heteroresistance. This card must not steal those failure modes; it should point at them.
Searching 'GeneXpert' alone redirected to the company in our ingest. Always cite the assay page, not Cepheid corporate history, when teaching TB.
deep: TrueNat and TB-LAMP are cousin WRDs on the clinic plate, not this product node.
Xpert XDR is a different cartridge (tb-xpert-xdr).
Cycle-threshold folklore as a 'load' is not a CFU and not DST.
WHO policy of mWRD-first is a programme object, not a Wikipedia timeline.

visual.caption: What the named classic MTB/RIF cartridge looked at: an rpoB RRDR window plus MTBC detection. Ultra's extra IS targets live on the clinic plate.
